runAssessment.summary: The run delivered a correct, self-contained linguistic analysis covering the lexicon, morphology, eight glosses, requested translations, evidential limits, and an alternative grammar, and root validation approved it. However, the $0.239589 spend over 355 seconds included four sequential phases that repeatedly asked the same L1 actor to produce substantially the complete answer, making a material portion of the work avoidably redundant despite the successful outcome.

findings.title: Sequential decomposition repeatedly regenerated the complete analysis
findings.detail: The tissue nominally separated evidence normalization, grammar induction, translation, and independent validation, but each downstream L1 task expanded back into a near-complete answer containing all glosses, all translations, caveats, and the alternative grammar. Four separate Protoplast plans and four Adrenaline plan/execute cycles followed. Choosing when dependent text-reasoning phases should reuse prior output versus regenerate a full deliverable requires a decomposition or synthesis policy decision; the trace does not establish an existing contract that was violated.

runAssessment.summary: The run delivered the requested MIDI, CSV, generator, verifier, and documentation for $0.23458108 over 814 seconds. Two initial verification failures exposed and corrected a MIDI-parser bug and an out-of-range bass note; the subsequent independent probe passed, the artifacts were read back, and root validation accepted all constraints. A missing final JSON envelope caused one recovery execution and some duplicated inspection, but it did not consume enough of the total spend to make the run substantially wasteful.

findings.title: Successful work required a redundant envelope-recovery execution
findings.detail: The primary build execution completed the artifacts and reached a passing probe but did not emit the required final JSON envelope. Recovery then reread the artifacts, regenerated them, and reran the already-passing verifier. The recovery call cost $0.0315, about 13% of total recorded spend; notable, but not enough on this single run to support a policy or code change.
